1.contenido: 1. The pastoral care of children's baptism has been greatly favored with the promulgation of the new Ritual, prepared according to the guidelines of the Second Vatican Council[1]. However, the difficulties warned by Christian parents and pastors of souls in the face of a rapid transformation of society, which makes the education of faith and the perseverance of young people more difficult, have not been completely dissipated.

2.contenido: 2. Many parents, in fact, are distressed to see their children abandoning faith and sacramental practice, despite the Christian education that they have tried to give them, and some pastors of souls wonder if they should not be more demanding before baptizing children. Some consider it preferable to defer the baptism of children until the end of a catechumenate of more or less duration; Others, however, ask that the doctrine on the necessity of baptism be revised—at least as it relates to children—and wish that the celebration of baptism be postponed until an age when a personal commitment is possible, or even until the threshold of adulthood.

3.contenido: 3. Given this situation, and to respond to numerous questions that have been addressed to it, the Sacred Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith, after having consulted various Episcopal Conferences, has prepared this Instruction. With it, it is proposed to remember the essential points of the Church's doctrine in this field, which justify the constant praxis of the Church throughout the centuries, and which demonstrate its permanent value, despite the difficulties that currently arise. Finally, some broad lines for pastoral action will be indicated.

4.contenido: 4. In both the East and the West, the practice of baptizing children is considered a norm of immemorial tradition. Origen, and later Saint Augustine, see in it a "tradition received from the Apostles"[2]. When the first direct testimonies appear in the second century, none of them ever present the baptism of children as an innovation. Saint Irenaeus, in particular, considers obvious the presence among the baptized "of small children and infants", alongside adolescents, young people and adults[3]. The oldest known ritual, which describes the Apostolic Tradition at the beginning of the 3rd century, contains the following prescription: «Children will be baptized first; all those who can speak alone, let them speak; For those who cannot do it, let their parents, or someone in their family, speak»[4]. Saint Cyprian, in a Synod of African Bishops, stated "that the mercy and grace of God cannot be denied to any man who comes into existence"; and the same Synod, invoking the "spiritual equality" of all men "of any stature and age", decreed that children could be baptized "from the second or third day after birth"[5].

5.contenido: 5. Undoubtedly, the practice of infant baptism experienced a certain regression during the 4th century. At that time, when adults themselves postponed their Christian initiation, for fear of future faults and for fear of public penance, many parents deferred, for the same reasons, the baptism of their children. But at the same time it is known that there were Fathers and Doctors, such as Basil, Gregory Nicene, Ambrose, John Chrysostom, Jerome, Augustine, who, although baptized in adulthood for the same reasons, nevertheless immediately reacted with energy, insistently asking adults not to delay the baptism necessary for salvation[6]; and many of them insisted that baptism also be administered to children[7].

6.contenido: 6. Popes and Councils also often intervened to remind Christians of the duty to have their children baptized.

7.contenido: 7. This doctrine was regularly reaffirmed and defended during the Middle Ages. In particular, the Council of Vienna, held in 1312, emphasizes that the effect of the sacrament of baptism on both children and adults is not only the remission of sins, but also the gift of grace and virtues[12]. The Council of Florence, in 1442, censures those who seek to defer this sacrament, and asks that baptism be conferred "as soon as possible" ( [+[0]+] ) on newborns, "by which they are removed from the power of the devil and receive the adoption of children of God"[13].

8.contenido: 8. The different regional Councils and Synods after the Council of Trent also firmly taught the need to baptize children. Very opportunely, Pope Paul VI solemnly recalled secular teaching on this point, declaring that, "baptism must also be administered to little ones who have not yet been able to become guilty of any personal sin, so that, born without supernatural grace, they may be reborn by water and the Holy Spirit to divine life in Christ Jesus"[17].

9.contenido: 9. The Magisterium texts cited now were above all about avoiding errors; They are far from exhausting the richness of the doctrine on baptism, as expressed in the New Testament, in the catechesis of the Fathers and in the teaching of the Doctors of the Church: baptism is a manifestation of the free love of the Father, participation in the paschal mystery of the Son, communication of a new life in the Spirit; Baptism brings men into the inheritance of God and adds them to the Body of Christ, which is the Church.

10.contenido: 10. In this perspective, Christ's warning in the Gospel of Saint John: "Whoever is not born of water and the Spirit cannot enter the kingdom of heaven"[18], must be understood as the invitation of a universal and infinite love; They are the words of a Father who calls his children and wants the greatest good for them. This irrevocable and urgent call cannot leave man in an indifferent or neutral attitude, since its acceptance is for him the condition of the fulfillment of his destiny.

11.contenido: 11. The Church must respond to the mission given by Christ to the Apostles after the resurrection, and described in the Gospel according to Saint Matthew in a particularly solemn way: «All power in heaven and on earth has been given to me; go then; Teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit"[19]. The transmission of the faith and the administration of baptism, closely linked in this command of the Lord, form an integral part of the mission of the Church, which is and cannot fail to be universal.

12.contenido: 12. This is how the Church has understood it from the earliest times, and not only with respect to adults. Reading the words of Jesus to Nicodemus, the Church "has always understood that children should not be deprived of baptism"[20]. Such words have in fact such a general and absolute form that the Fathers have collected them to establish the need for baptism, and the Magisterium has expressly applied them to the case of children[21]: for them too, this sacrament is the entrance into the People of God[22] and the door to personal salvation.

13.contenido: 13. Therefore, through its doctrine and its praxis, the Church has taught that it knows no other means than baptism to assure children's entry into eternal blessedness; For this reason, she tries not to neglect the mission she has received from the Lord to make all those who can be baptized "reborn of water and the Spirit." Regarding children who have died without having received baptism, the Church can do no more than entrust them to the mercy of God, as it does in the funeral rite that it has arranged for them[23].

14.contenido: 14. The fact that children cannot yet personally profess their faith does not prevent the Church from conferring this sacrament on them, because in reality, it baptizes them into their own faith. This doctrinal point was already clearly established by Saint Augustine, who wrote: «Children are presented to receive spiritual grace, not so much by those who carry them in their arms ([+[0]+]), but by the universal society of saints and the faithful... It is the entire Mother Church that acts in her saints: because all of her generates each and every one»[24]. Saint Thomas Aquinas, and after him all theologians, follow the same teaching: the child who is baptized does not believe by himself, through a personal act, but through others, "by the faith of the Church that is communicated to him"[25]. This same doctrine is expressed in the new Ritual of Baptism, when the celebrant asks the parents, godfathers and godmothers, to profess the faith of the Church "in which children are baptized"[26].

15.contenido: 15. However, the Church, although aware of the effectiveness of her faith that acts in the baptism of children and the validity of the sacrament that she confers on them, recognizes limits to her praxis, since, except in the case of danger of death, she does not accept giving the sacrament without the consent of the parents and the serious guarantee that the baptized child will receive a Catholic education[27]; In fact, the Church is concerned both with the natural rights of parents and with the requirement of the development of faith in the child.

16.contenido: 16. In light of the doctrine recalled above, certain opinions currently expressed regarding the baptism of children and which tend to call into question its legitimacy as a general rule must be judged.

17.contenido: 17. Taking into account that, in the writings of the New Testament, baptism follows the preaching of the Gospel, which involves conversion and is accompanied by the profession of faith and that, furthermore, the effects of grace ([+[0]+] ) are generally linked to faith rather than to the sacrament[28], some propose that the successive stages "preaching-faith-sacrament" be established as a norm. Except, then, in cases of danger of death, it would have to be applied to children and a mandatory catechumenate established for them.

18.contenido: 18. Certainly, apostolic preaching was normally addressed to adults and the first baptized were men converted to the Christian faith. Since these events are narrated by the New Testament, this could lead one to think that only the faith of adults is considered in them. However, as recalled above, the praxis of infant baptism is based on an immemorial tradition, of apostolic origin, whose value cannot be discarded; Furthermore, baptism has never been administered without faith: for children, it is the faith of the Church.

19.contenido: 19. It is also said that all grace, since it is intended for a person, must be consciously accepted and made his own by the person who receives it, of which the child is incapable.

20.contenido: 20. In reality, the child is a person long before he is capable of manifesting it through conscious and free acts, and as such, he can already become, through the sacrament of baptism, a son of God and a joint heir with Christ. His conscience and his freedom will then be able, from his awakening, to dispose of the energies infused into his soul by baptismal grace.

21.contenido: 21. It is also objected that the baptism of children would be an attack on their freedom. It would be contrary to their dignity as a person to impose on them religious obligations for the future that, later, they could perhaps reject. It would be better not to confer the sacrament until an age when free commitment is possible. In the meantime, parents and educators should behave with reserve and refrain from all pressure.

22.contenido: 22. But such an attitude is absolutely illusory: there is no such thing as pure human freedom that is exempt from all conditioning. Already on the natural level, parents make choices for their children that are essential for their lives and their orientation towards true values. A supposedly neutral attitude of the family towards the child's religious life would in fact be a negative option, which would deprive the child of an essential good.

23.contenido: 23. Attentive to the link between the person and society, some believe that, in a homogeneous society, where values, judgments and customs form a coherent system, the baptism of children is still appropriate; but this praxis would be contraindicated in current pluralistic societies, characterized by the instability of values ​​and conflicts of ideas. In this situation, it would be advisable to wait until the candidate's personality was sufficiently mature.

24.contenido: 24. The Church is undoubtedly aware that it must take into account the social base. But the criteria of homogeneity and pluralism are only indicative and cannot be established as normative principles; because they are inadequate to resolve a properly religious issue that, by its nature, concerns the Church and the Christian family.

25.contenido: 25. Finally, there is another criticism of the baptism of children: it would derive from a pastoral ministry lacking missionary impulse, more concerned with administering a sacrament than with awakening faith and promoting evangelical commitment. By maintaining it, the Church would give in to the temptation of numbers and social "institution"; It would encourage the maintenance of a "magical conception" of the sacraments, while its duty is to point towards missionary activity, to mature the faith of Christians, to promote their free and conscious commitment, and as a consequence to admit stages in their sacramental pastoral care.

26.contenido: 26. Without a doubt, the apostolate of the Church must tend to raise a living faith and promote a truly Christian existence; But the demands of the sacramental pastoral care of adults cannot simply be applied to young children who are baptized, as has been recalled before, "in the faith of the Church." Furthermore, the need for the sacrament, which maintains all its value and urgency, should not be treated lightly, especially when it comes to assuring a child of the infinite good of eternal life.

27.contenido: 27. If it is not possible to accept some current propositions, such as the definitive abandonment of the baptism of children and the freedom of choice - whatever the reasons - between immediate baptism and deferred baptism, the need for a profound pastoral effort, and in certain aspects renewed, cannot nevertheless be denied. It is convenient to indicate here the principles and the main lines.

28.contenido: 28. It is important to remember from the beginning that the baptism of children must be considered a serious mission. The questions that this poses to pastors can only be resolved with faithful attention to the doctrine and constant practice of the Church.

29.contenido: 29. Based on these two principles, reflection on specific cases will be done through a pastoral dialogue between the priest and the family. For dialogue with parents who are habitually practicing Christians, the norms are established in the introduction of the Ritual. Suffice it to remember now the two most significant points.

30.contenido: 30. Pastors may find themselves faced with parents who are little believers and occasional practitioners or even non-Christian parents who, for reasons worthy of consideration, request baptism for their children.

31.contenido: 31. These regulations, already promulgated and currently in force[41], require some clarifications.

32.contenido: 32. The pastoral effort deployed on the occasion of the baptism of children must be inserted into a broader action, extended to families and the entire Christian community.

33.contenido: 33. As the Ritual clearly indicates, the parish community, and in particular the group of Christians who form the human environment of the home, must have their place in this pastoral care of baptism. In fact, given that the People of God, which is the Church, transmits and nourishes the faith received from the Apostles, it is incumbent on them to be eminently interested in preparation for baptism and in Christian education[44]. This active intervention of the Christian People, already put into practice when it comes to adults, serves for the baptism of children, because "the People of God, which is the Church, represented by the local community, also has an important role to play"[45]. Furthermore, the community itself will normally derive great spiritual and apostolic benefit from the baptism ceremony. Finally, its action after the liturgical celebration will continue in the help provided by adults for the education of the faith of young people, both through the testimony of their Christian life and through their participation in various catechetical activities.

34.contenido: 34. In addressing the bishops, the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith has full confidence that, in the exercise of the mission received from the Lord, they will make every effort to remember the doctrine of the Church on the need for the baptism of children, to promote adequate pastoral care, and to guide back toward traditional praxis those who, perhaps due to understandable pastoral concerns, have distanced themselves from it. Likewise, he hopes that the teaching and guidelines of this Instruction reach all pastors, Christian parents and the ecclesial community, so that everyone becomes aware of their responsibilities and contributes, through the baptism of children and their Christian education, to the growth of the Church, the Body of Christ.
